name: Remote Backup
author: Bo Reese (bobreese)
description: Designate an FPP as a Backup Host and pull rsync backups of one or more MultiSync remotes onto local NVMe/SSD, USB, or SD card storage. Configurable concurrent transfers (up to 8), --dry-run space checks, mirrored deletes, and dated/rolling per-remote backups named like Pi5-20260803.

privacy.summary: Pulls backups from FPP systems you select over SSH onto this device's storage. Optionally emails a status update through FPP's own Email settings after each run.

sends.what: SSH authentication and rsync transfer commands - pulls content only, never sends show data out

sends.to: the address in FPP Settings > Email
sends.what: a short status summary (which remotes succeeded, failed, or were skipped)
sends.why: to notify the operator after a backup run without them checking the Status page

collects.what: a full copy of each selected remote's media folder, which can include its saved passwords/tokens
collects.where: the backup destination you configure, in <Hostname>-<date>/

collects.what: a copy of that remote's OS-level network config, including its WiFi password, if enabled
collects.where: the backup destination you configure, in <Hostname>-<date>/system-config.tar.gz

collects.what: a default SSH password, if you set one

systemChanges.what: pushes its own SSH key to each selected remote for passwordless access; best-effort removes it on uninstall
sets FPP's restartFlag after install/uninstall so its Scheduler commands register/unregister
mounts a USB drive at /mnt/Backups (and optionally /mnt/BackupsCopy) via /etc/fstab for use as a backup destination
installs rsync, jq, openssh-client, sshpass, curl, parted, zip, and exfatprogs via apt-get if not already present

privacy.other: A settings backup file (plugindata/fpp-plugin-RemoteBackup/settings.json.bak) is left behind after uninstall by default, so a reinstall can recover your configuration - remove it yourself, or re-run the uninstall script with --purge-backups, if you want it gone too. The SSH key push only happens for a remote you've selected to back up, never automatically for every discovered device - the Config page's Remote Systems section discloses this at the point of selection. The full media-tree copy in collects above can include that remote's own FPP settings file (UI login, OS, SMTP/email, and MQTT passwords, a GitHub personal access token, and a tethering PSK, all in plain text) and other installed plugins' own stored data, which may include their own API keys or tokens.
